notes: Checks from the contract's table (engine/collision.md#spike-testsenginecollision, Technical Director 2026-10-01), measured by the raster-engineer in M4 stage 2 (2026-10-02; figures and how they were taken: engine/collision.md#results, tests/engine/collision/measure.py). The spike cycles through three phases every 256 frames: M moving (224 frames), W the contract's worst mix held static (16), B the same layout with no tests, so that the border passes run with nothing else in the frame (16). The five 'border' checks are locks: constant paths run from line 252 on in phase B frames, no badline, no sprite DMA, no IRQ inside, so min_cycles = max_cycles = the measured figure; 32 samples = two whole cycles of the spike. Their spans are a jsr to the instruction after it, so they are WHOLE CALLS (profile span + jsr 6 + rts 6: engine/README.md#which-span-a-figure-is). TWO DEPARTURES from the contract's table, both reported to the Technical Director: (1) its first row, collision_begin -> collision_begin_end with limit 90, cannot be a lock on those labels, because the spike must also call collision_begin in the display (four times a frame, in spike_collide), where DMA lands on it (83-183 measured). It is locked here as the border call spike_begin -> spike_begin_end = 95 = 83 + 12; the contract's 90 is for the 83. (2) The worst frame through the display measures 2,335 against the contract's 2,100 (an estimate): the measured lock is 'max over 600 passes + 5%' as the contract says such a row becomes, and the 2,100 itself is kept as a separate check at from_stage 3, so it prints PENDING and fails under --strict until the Technical Director decides: the target is not moved here. 'stage': 2 = the spike as built in M4 stage 2. Schema: engine/README.md#budget-files.
